inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP6364 = FLIP_SWNO(63,64) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP6364 = FLIP_SWNO(63,64) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 64 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 64: a host write to 64 is overwritten on the next update. The table's key handler writes 64 directly and then calls de.vbs vpmKeyDown, whose swLRFlip is 82; the harness read back 64 = 1 only while 82 was held. The right cabinet button stack switches both the lower right and the upper right flipper on the 3-flipper board. mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest on subminiature switches 11 (left) to 14 (right) in the inclined trough under the right apron. Output 1, the lock-out cam, releases the ball at 14 toward the up-kicker; the remaining balls roll down one position. A ball at the up-kicker blocks opto 15, and output 2 lifts it into shooter lane 16. In the harness, the ROM fired 1 to serve, then 2 once 15 closed. The table models the trough as bsTrough (InitSw 0,14,13,12,11) and a separate bsBallRelease saucer at 15.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough and up-kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Shooter lane 16 feeds the autolaunch under the butyrate (output 3), which shoots the ball up the shooter lane ramp. On the first serve of a ball the ROM shows the skill-shot choice and launches when the cabinet gun trigger 49 is pulled; a ball served to replace a locked ball launched without the trigger. If 16 stays closed after launching, the ROM retries and reports OPERATOR ALERT! AUTOLAUNCH NOT WORKING.
mechanisms.label: Gun-trigger autolaunch

mechanisms.behavior: The upper-left saucer 41 holds a ball until output 5 kicks it out (0.17 s after 41 closed in the harness gameplay run); it starts lit Gotham Events.
mechanisms.label: Top eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: The upper-right vertical up-kicker 32 lifts a ball with output 4 (5.6 s after 32 closed in the harness gameplay run) up the wire ramp to the Batcave on the left side, where it reaches the lock stack 62/61/60.
mechanisms.label: VUK to the Batcave

mechanisms.behavior: The Batcave holds up to three balls on 62 (bottom), 61 (middle) and 60 (top). When the C-A-V-E bank has lit locks, a ball arriving at 62 is held and the ROM serves a replacement from the trough (observed: 62 closing answered by lock-out 1). Output 9 releases the bottom ball toward the Batcave exit kicker 30. The table models the lock as bsBallLock (InitSw 0,62,61,60) kicked out by 9.
mechanisms.label: Batcave ball lock

mechanisms.behavior: A ball at 30 is kicked by output 16 (0.93 s after 30 closed in the harness gameplay run) down the Batcave exit wire ramp over the lower arch onto the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Batcave exit kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Targets 18-21 (C, A, V, E) latch down independently and stay closed while down. Output 7 resets the whole bank; in the harness gameplay run it fired 0.2 s after the fourth target dropped. The table raises all four with DTRaise.
mechanisms.label: C-A-V-E four-target drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Output 12 moves the Bridge Diverter on the double stack wire ramp that leaves the left/middle ramp: energized, it sends a left-ramp ball (entering at 52) down the lower wire ramp to the Batwing Cannon, where it closes 44; at rest the ball continues on the upper wire. Rules: ARM BATWING lit on the left ramp loads the cannon. The table makes RampDiverter non-collidable while 12 is on.
mechanisms.label: Batwing ramp diverter

mechanisms.behavior: A ball delivered to the cannon closes 44. The ROM then energizes motor relay 14 (about 2 s after 44 in the harness), and the AC motor swings the cannon through a crank and cam links; home switch 46 marks the home position on the drive. Pulling the cabinet gun trigger 49 fires output 15 (about 0.1 s later), shooting the ball the way the cannon points. During FOREVER the cannon oscillates and a ball must be caught as it passes home. Switch 45 BATWING CANNON SAFETY is on the assembly, but no source says what it senses. The table drives the swing with a cvpmMech on 14 (500 ms per 200 steps, reversing, 46 closed at both ends).
mechanisms.label: Batwing cannon

mechanisms.behavior: Left, bottom and right switches 57, 58 and 59 fire special-solenoid outputs 17, 18 and 19 within milliseconds in the harness.
mechanisms.label: Three turbo bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left 35 and right 36 fire outputs 20 and 21 within milliseconds in the harness.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: When the feature is lit, left outlane switch 33 fires output 22 (within 10 ms in the harness), kicking the ball back up the outlane from under the arch. Completing the top lanes relights it.
mechanisms.label: Left outlane Laser Kick

mechanisms.behavior: Three flippers: lower left (22-1080), lower right (22-900) and upper right (23-900) on the solid state 3-flipper board 520-5076-00. The left cabinet button enables the lower left flipper; the right button stack enables both right flippers. Only the lower flippers have N.C. EOS switches; the upper flipper's EOS is printed Not Used. PinMAME copies 82/84 to matrix 64/63 and fabricates 45/46 and 47/48 in pairs, so use one state per side. No CPU driver reaches the flipper board.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet-controlled flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Output 8 pulses the cabinet knocker 500-5081-00; it has no playfield sensor or placement.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet knocker

mechanisms.behavior: Relay 10 on the PPB switches drives 1-8 between the coil loads 1L-8L and the flasher loads 1R-8R (25-32). Relay 11 on the power supply board switches the G.I. supply; the table's G.I. is lit while 11 is off.
mechanisms.label: PPB bank selection and G.I. control

physical.notes: Driver chart 1L: 4-BALL LOCKOUT. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #1L: 4-BALL LOCKOUT with CPU CN11-P1 Q46 and fires this address alone. The 25-1240 coil of the Lock Ball Assembly 500-5684-01 releases one ball from trough position 14 toward the up-kicker; the table has no object for it.

Driver chart 2L: TROUGH UP-KICKER. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #2L: TROUGH UP KICKER with CPU CN11-P3 Q45 and fires this address alone. The 23-800 up-kicker at the trough's upper end lifts the ball past opto 15 into shooter lane 16.

Driver chart 3L: AUTOLAUNCH 50V. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #3L: AUTOLAUNCH 50V with CPU CN11-P4 Q44 and fires this address alone. Autolaunch Assembly 500-5477-01 under the butyrate at the shooter lane. On the first serve the ROM waits for the gun trigger (skill shot); later serves launched without it.

Driver chart 4L: VUK 50V. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #4L: VUK 50V with CPU CN11-P5 Q43 and fires this address alone. Vertical Up-Kicker Assembly 500-5839-01 at the upper right; the ball goes up the wire ramp to the Batcave.

Driver chart 5L: TOP EJECT. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #5L: TOP EJECT with CPU CN11-P6 Q42 and fires this address alone. Ball Eject (Saucer) Assembly 500-5664-00 at the upper left, the Gotham Event saucer. The factory drawing (Sega_1995_Batman_Forever_Manual_with_schematics_duplicate_pages_33_34_missing_pages_143_144.pdf PDF 33, printed 27) ends callout 5L's leader 0.196 normalized from it, beyond the 0.07 limit, so this placement stays observed.

Driver chart row 6L is printed shaded NOT USED with Q41, VIO-BLU and PPB J2-6 but dashes for the coil. The coil wiring diagram (PDF 108) prints "NO COIL AT THIS LOCATION Q41CPU 6L". The ROM's own diagnostics publish state here: CYCLING COILS pulses 6 while it displays #6L: NOT USED, and the COIL TEST shows #6L: NOT USED without a RUN entry. No gameplay or attract run published it. The diagnostics walk every driver slot, so this state drives no load.

Driver chart 7L: 4-BANK DROP TARGET RESET. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #7L: 4-BANK DROP TARGET RESET with CPU CN11-P8 Q40 and fires this address alone. One reset coil for the 4-Bank Drop Target Assembly 500-5799-04; its placement is projected onto the mean of the four target primitives, not a measured coil centre. The Tech Chart prints 50v L; the manual and the ROM's BRN 32V DC agree on 32v.
Driver chart 8L: KNOCKER. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #8L: KNOCKER with CPU CN11-P9 Q39 and fires this address alone. Knocker Assembly 500-5081-00 in the cabinet.

Driver chart 9: BATCAVE BALL LOCK. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #9: BATCAVE BALL LOCK with CPU CN12-P1 Q30 and fires this address alone. Batcave Ball Lock 500-5947-00-38 on the left side: releases the bottom ball of the three-ball lock stack 62/61/60 toward the Batcave exit kicker.

Driver chart 10: LEFT & RIGHT (A/B) RELAY Loc: PPB (Not Shown in Display). K1 A/B relay on the PPB selects the 1L-8L coil loads (off) or the 1R-8R flasher loads (on) on drives 1-8; these are eight shared drivers with alternate loads. The COIL TEST has no entry for it.

Driver chart 11: G.I. RELAY Loc: Power Supply. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #11: G.I. RELAY with CPU CN12-P4 Q28 and fires this address alone. A 24v DC relay on the power supply board switches the 6.3 VAC G.I. supply; the ROM's COIL TEST prints its PS traces. The table hides its G.I. lights while the relay is energized. Placements are the table's G.I. bulb lights; the physical socket count and string allocation are not settled.

Driver chart 12: BATWING RAMP DIVERTER. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #12: BATWING RAMP DIVERTER with CPU CN12-P5 Q27 and fires this address alone. Ramp Diverter Assembly 500-5940-00-38 (27-1500 coil) moves the Bridge Diverter on the Double Stack Wire Ramp 500-5932-00-38, sending a left-ramp ball down the lower wire ramp to the Batwing Cannon. The factory drawing (Sega_1995_Batman_Forever_Manual_with_schematics_duplicate_pages_33_34_missing_pages_143_144.pdf PDF 33, printed 27) ends callout 12's leader 0.076 normalized from it, beyond the 0.07 limit, so this placement stays observed.

Driver chart row 13 is printed shaded NOT USED with Q26, BRN-GRN and CPU CN12-6 but dashes for the coil. The coil wiring diagram (PDF 108) draws loads only on CPU CN12 pins 1, 5 and 7, none on CN12-6, and the 3-flipper board takes no CPU driver. The ROM's own diagnostics publish state here: RUN on #13: NOT USED in the COIL TEST holds 13 on until the selection moves, and CYCLING COILS holds it for about 2.5 s while displaying #13: NOT USED. No gameplay or attract run published it. The diagnostics walk every driver slot, so this state drives no load.

Driver chart 14: BATWING MOTOR RELAY. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #14: BATWING MOTOR RELAY with CPU CN12-P7 Q25 and fires this address alone. Not a solenoid: the driver energizes a 24v DC 10A DPDT relay on relay board 520-5010-00 (part number printed by the ROM and the Tech Chart) whose N.O. contact switches 28 VAC from BR2 to the Cannon Motor Drive Assembly 500-6018-00-38 (motor 515-6383-00). Through a crank and cam links the motor swings the Batwing Cannon; home switch 46 sits on the drive.

Driver chart 15: BATWING CANNON 50V. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #15: BATWING CANNON 50V with CPU CN12-P8 Q24 and fires this address alone. The 23-800 coil and plunger of the Batwing Cannon Assembly 515-6321-00-38 fire a ball loaded at 44 in the direction the cannon points.
